questions.q: Examine the state of human development in India and the regional disparities in it.
answer: Human development in India, measured through health, education and income, has improved over the years but remains uneven across the country.

answer.text: India falls in the medium human development category. Life expectancy and literacy have risen and per capita income has grown, yet infant mortality, malnutrition and gender inequality remain matters of concern in many areas.

The level of human development varies greatly between states. Kerala stands at the top, with high literacy, good health services, a favourable sex ratio and low infant mortality, showing that investment in education and health raises human development. In contrast, several states in the north and centre lag behind on these indicators.
Wide gaps also exist between rural and urban areas, between men and women, and between social groups such as the Scheduled Castes and Tribes and the rest.

answer: Thus, while India has progressed, reducing these disparities is essential for balanced human development.
